c1.note: Reports say layoffs began Sept 14 and WARN notices dated that day plus March round support a second major round; the BI 'confirmed' wording is not directly visible but is consistent.

c5.note: Four filings, 800 workers, effective Nov 13, 2026, recorded Sept 14; the layoffs are described as permanent.

c8.note: 359 in Washington and 441 in California (279+99+63) confirmed by multiple sources and the WA ESD filing.

c9.note: Pleasanton 63, Redwood City 279 and Santa Clara 99 sum to 441, all effective Nov 13, 2026.

c10.note: The 279/99/63 breakdown matches the WARN listings.

c11.note: TheStreet says the tally covers only public state WARN notices and is not a global total; CIO also notes no verified headcount.

c12.note: The 10-Q states total estimated costs of up to $2.1 billion as of Aug 31, 2026.

c13.note: The 10-Q says management supplemented the plan by about $700M after Aug 31; Bloomberg and CIO date the filing to Sept 11.

c14.note: The 10-Q states $167M and $415M of restructuring expenses for the 2026 plan for the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 and 2025.

c15.note: The 10-Q text mentions adoption and integration of AI technologies across certain functions, and says changes to estimates will be reflected in future results.

c17.note: Business Insider and the 10-K figures show 162,000 to 141,000, down 21,000 or 13%.

c18.note: The 10-K states approximately 141,000 full-time employees as of May 31, 2026.

c20.note: Business Insider describes the leaked document as listing 546 laid-off employees, about 7.6% of 7,185.

c21.note: Business Insider says managers, engineers, software developers and data center maintenance and servicing workers were most affected, but this applies to the cloud infrastructure org rather than all of Oracle's cuts.

c22.note: Oracle has not disclosed total affected, and Business Insider and the CIO article agree there is no solid headcount; this may have changed since.

c23.note: Seattle Times reports 741 Seattle-area employees from Aug 2025 to March, about 1,100 with the September cuts.

c24.note: Seattle Times quotes the filing language that AI adoption has led to workforce reductions, and Indmoney says the same of the annual report.

c25.note: WARNact page states 11 notices, 5 states, 2,207 workers, May 7, 2025 to Sep 14, 2026.

c26.note: Notices were filed Sep 14 with effective date Nov 13, so as of Nov 11 they are still pending; workers remain employed until then.

c27.note: Business Engineer reports 1,977 jobs in 8 CA and WA notices (1,177 spring + 800 September); this is a secondary tally.

c28.note: Source says the count covers only CA and WA notices meeting WARN thresholds and excludes Texas and others, so it is not a global total.

c29.note: TheStreet reports about $1.8B in FY2026 restructuring costs, and the 10-Q confirms up to $2.1B total as of Aug 31, 2026.

c31.note: CNBC video headline 'Oracle laying off thousands of employees, sources' and article on Mar 31 confirm.

c34.note: Oracle did not disclose affected count; figures come from WARN notices and reports, and Oracle only disclosed restructuring costs and headcount in filings.

c35.note: WARN notice text states notification on or before September 14, 2026.

c36.note: Notice states separation on November 13, 2026, two days from today.

c37.note: Letter dated September 14, 2026 and stamped received 9/14/2026.

c38.note: BBC 1 April 2026: Oracle made 'significant' job cuts on Tuesday, per senior employees posting online.

c39.note: BBC: 'Some 10,000 people are believed to have lost their jobs so far, one employee told the BBC'; an unconfirmed estimate.

c40.note: BBC: 'Oracle declined to comment when contacted by BBC News.'

c41.note: TheStreet: WARN notices document at least 2,578 U.S. cuts, not a global total.

c42.note: Reuters Mar 5, 2026 headline: Oracle plans thousands of job cuts, citing Bloomberg.

c44.note: No Oracle release with a layoff count appears; Oracle did not confirm figures, consistent with the other sources.

c47.note: Sources show Nov 13, 2026 WARN-listed Oracle layoffs in WA and CA, though these are effective dates of the Sept round notices, not a new round; the claim of no later round is plausible but the sources are mixed and the claim is not clearly supported.

c48.note: CIO quotes the analyst saying the $700M supplement covers termination benefits and contract termination and exit costs and cannot be divided into people.

c49.note: TheStreet text says exactly this about the Washington WARN notice, and GeekWire confirms the Seattle sites are not closing.

c50.note: The first-round total of 1,778 across WA 475, CA 702, MO 539 and NY 62, with separations from May 26 to June 1, matches the passage.

c51.note: INDmoney says the reports of another 7,000 to 10,000 positions have not been confirmed by Oracle.

c52.note: TD Cowen's January note estimated 20,000 to 30,000 cuts, and CIO says the 30,000 was a forecast and not confirmed by Oracle.

c4.note: The saved Business Insider page says employees were offered 4 weeks' base salary plus 1 week per year of employment, citing documents it viewed.

c30.note: A web search found that the March 2026 10-Q raised the plan by $500M to $2.1B. The saved INDmoney page dates the $2.1B figure to August instead, and the later September increase of about $700M supersedes it.

c43.note: The saved Reuters text has no 'declined to comment' line. CNBC and BBC report that Oracle declined to comment to them, not to Reuters.

c53.note: The INDmoney blog says the restructuring budget was raised to about $2.8B, which matches the roughly $700M added to the $2.1B plan.
